title: Madam Rides the Bus (poem: The Tale of Custard the Dragon)

topics.title: A child's curiosity: reporting commands and requests

learn.hook: What is so exciting about a bus ride? Ask any child who has watched the world rush past the window!
points: In 'Madam Rides the Bus' by Vallikkannan, a curious village girl, Valli, longs to ride the bus to town. She saves her coins carefully and makes the trip on her own.
Her curiosity, careful planning and confidence make her a lively young 'madam'. The journey also teaches her something about life.
Reported commands and requests use: told/ordered/requested/advised/warned + person + to + verb.
Negative commands use 'not to': 'Don't lean out' → He warned me not to lean out.
'Please' is dropped; its meaning goes into the verb 'requested'.

example.q: Passage: Chintu pressed his nose to the bus window in Chennai. 'Uncle, please open the window wider,' he said to the conductor. 'Don't lean out,' the conductor warned, smiling. Report what Chintu said to the conductor.
steps: It is a polite request ('please'), so use 'requested'.
Drop 'please' and use 'to' + verb: to open.
'Uncle' is a form of address and is dropped; 'the conductor' becomes the object.
example.answer: Chintu requested the conductor to open the window wider.

learn.reallife: Signboards and instructions are commands in short form: 'Do not lean out of the window', 'Please stand in a queue.'

items.text: The conductor warned Chintu ___ lean out.
Valli requested the conductor ___ her a window seat.
The doctor advised Papa ___ walk every day.
The teacher ___ the class to be quiet.

quiz.q: In 'Madam Rides the Bus', what is Valli's greatest wish?
options: To ride the bus to the town
quiz.explain: Valli longs to travel on the bus she watches every day.
quiz.mistake: Gives a common childhood wish not from the story

quiz.q: How does Valli get the money for her bus ride?
options: Her mother gives it to her
She saves her coins carefully over a long time
The conductor lets her ride free
She borrows it from a neighbour
quiz.explain: She saves every coin and resists spending on treats.
quiz.mistake: Assumes an adult paid for her

quiz.q: Passage: Chintu pressed his nose to the bus window in Chennai. 'Uncle, please open the window wider,' he said to the conductor. 'Don't lean out,' the conductor warned, smiling. Report what the conductor said.
options: The conductor warned Chintu don't lean out.
The conductor warned Chintu to not leaning out.
The conductor warned Chintu not to lean out.
The conductor said Chintu not lean out.
quiz.explain: Negative command: warned + person + not to + verb.

quiz.q: Passage: Chintu pressed his nose to the bus window in Chennai. 'Uncle, please open the window wider,' he said to the conductor. 'Don't lean out,' the conductor warned, smiling. Report what Chintu said.
options: Chintu requested the conductor please open the window wider.
Chintu ordered the conductor to open the window wider.
Chintu said the conductor opens the window wider.
Chintu requested the conductor to open the window wider.
quiz.explain: 'Please' signals a request; the reporting verb 'requested' replaces it.
quiz.mistake: Keeps 'please' or uses a verb that changes the tone

quiz.q: Report: Mother said to me, 'You should carry water.'
options: Mother advised me to carry water.
Mother advised me that carry water.
Mother requested me to carried water.
quiz.explain: 'Should' gives advice, so 'advised + to + verb' is used.
quiz.mistake: Does not match the reporting verb to the meaning

quiz.q: Which reporting verb best suits a polite request?
quiz.mistake: Uses a verb that sounds like a command

quiz.explain: A curious person wants to find out about things.

quiz.q: What is the noun form of 'curious'?
quiz.explain: The noun is 'curiosity' (note the spelling: no 'u' after 's').
quiz.mistake: Picks the adverb or misspells the noun

teach.ask: Gappu: Mama Bird said, 'Don't fly near the road!' How do I tell my brother what she said?
teach.praise: Chirp! 'Mama warned us not to fly near the road.' Use 'not to' for a 'don't'. Brother, listen!
teach.nudge: What words come after 'warned us' when the command starts with 'Don't'?

topics.title: A humorous ballad: Custard the Dragon

learn.hook: A dragon who is scared of everything? That sounds like the funniest hero ever!
points: 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon' by Ogden Nash is a humorous ballad about Belinda and her pets: Ink the kitten, Blink the mouse, Mustard the dog, and Custard, a 'cowardly' dragon.
Everyone teases Custard for being a coward, but when a pirate arrives, he is the one who fights while the others hide: a funny twist that shows true courage.
A ballad is a poem that tells a story, usually in short stanzas with a regular rhyme and rhythm, often with repetition.
This ballad rhymes in couplets: aabb.
Humour comes from exaggeration, made-up words, funny names and the surprise ending.

example.q: Ballad: In Madurai lived a girl named Meera, / With a parrot called Pista and a goat called Heera, / And a timid old buffalo, slow as a snail, / Who once chased a thief all the way to the jail! Find the rhyme scheme and the funny twist.
steps: The twist: a 'timid', snail-slow buffalo is the one who chases a thief.
example.answer: The rhyme scheme is aabb; the humour is that the timid, slow buffalo turns out to be the hero.

learn.reallife: Folk songs and storytelling traditions across India, from Rajasthan to Assam, tell tales in rhyming verse, much like ballads.

games.title: Ballad facts
items: 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon' was written by Ogden Nash.
Ogden Nash is known for funny verse.
In the poem, Custard runs away when the pirate comes.
Custard fights the pirate while the others hide.
The poem rhymes in couplets, aabb.
A humorous ballad cannot have a message.
Custard's story shows that real courage is shown when it matters.

quiz.q: Who wrote 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon'?
quiz.explain: Ogden Nash wrote this funny ballad.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the humorous poets of the book

options: A poem with no rhyme at all
A poem that tells a story, usually in rhyming stanzas
A short poem of three lines
quiz.explain: Ballads are story poems with regular rhyme and rhythm.
quiz.mistake: Confuses ballad with other poem forms

quiz.q: How do the others describe Custard at the start?
quiz.explain: Custard is mocked for being a coward who cries for a safe cage.
quiz.mistake: Assumes dragons are always shown as brave

quiz.q: What is the name of Belinda's dog?
quiz.explain: Mustard is the dog; Ink is the kitten, Blink the mouse, Custard the dragon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the rhyming pet names

quiz.q: What is the rhyme scheme of 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon'?
quiz.explain: Each pair of lines rhymes: aabb.

quiz.q: Ballad: In Madurai lived a girl named Meera, / With a parrot called Pista and a goat called Heera, / And a timid old buffalo, slow as a snail, / Who once chased a thief all the way to the jail! What makes this ballad funny?
options: A timid, slow buffalo chases a thief to jail
quiz.explain: The surprise that the 'timid', slow buffalo becomes a hero is the joke.
quiz.mistake: Picks a plain detail instead of the twist

quiz.q: Ballad: In Madurai lived a girl named Meera, / With a parrot called Pista and a goat called Heera, / And a timid old buffalo, slow as a snail, / Who once chased a thief all the way to the jail! Which phrase is a simile?
options: all the way to the jail
quiz.mistake: Thinks any descriptive phrase is a simile

quiz.q: What is the funny twist in 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon'?
options: The mouse is the bravest of all
The 'cowardly' dragon is the only one who fights the pirate
quiz.explain: Those who boasted of courage hide, and Custard fights.
quiz.mistake: Forgets who actually faced the pirate

teach.ask: Gappu: Why is a story poem about a scaredy-cat dragon so funny? And what kind of poem is it?
teach.praise: Ha-chirp! It's a ballad, and the joke is that the 'coward' turns out bravest. Go, Custard!
teach.nudge: What kind of poem tells a story? And what surprise makes it funny?
